rounds.text: Sky Gold & Diamonds Ltd is exhibiting exceptional financial velocity, underscored by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 76% and a TTM sales expansion of 73% [E14, E15]. Profitability matches this top-line acceleration, with 3-year compounded profit growth reaching 144% and TTM profit growth scaling by 117% [E16, E17]. Operational efficiency is exceptionally high, delivering an ROE of 28.9% and an ROCE of 26.9%, which significantly outstrips sector benchmarks where sector median ROE sits at just 8.76% [E9, E12, E13]. Furthermore, the business is backed by institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings expanding substantially since December 2023 [E36, E37] alongside a positive institutional money flow signal [E38]. Management's strategic execution is equally robust, as demonstrated by the upward revision of FY27 revenue projections to approximately ₹8,100 crores while currently operating at only 60% capacity utilization, leaving massive room for expansion [E72, E83]. Conceded: The company currently offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and experienced negative operating cash flow of ₹45 crores in March 2026 [E4, E29].

Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E16], [E17], [E18], [E19], [E20], [E21], [E22], [E23], [E24], [E25], [E26], [E36], [E37], [E38], [E39], [E41], [E44], [E45], [E46], [E49], [E58], [E59], [E60], [E61], [E62], [E71], [E72], [E74], [E75], [E76], [E77], [E78], [E79], [E83], [E84], [E85]. Sky Gold & Diamonds Ltd trades at a rich P/E of 36.1 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 10.30x [E2], alongside a steep EV/EBITDA of 30.1x that dwarfs the sector benchmark of 13.83x [E11]. This expensive valuation coincides with alarming cash flow deterioration, evidenced by a negative cash conversion of -0.16x, an operating cash flow of Rs -45 Cr, and a staggering free cash flow of Rs -140 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E29, E30]. Compounding these operational risks, borrowings have climbed to Rs 964 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 869 Cr a year earlier [E33], while promoter holding has dropped by 10.34 percentage points to 51.74% [E35].

Conceded: [E28], [E29], [E30], [E33], and [E35]. The bear's fixation on rich valuation multiples like the 36.1 P/E and 10.30x P/B [E1, E2] ignores that top-tier operational efficiency commands a premium, as demonstrated by superior ROE of 28.9% and ROCE of 26.9% [E12, E13]. While EV/EBITDA is elevated against sector benchmarks [E11], the company is executing aggressively on its expansion roadmap, taking manufacturing footprint to 1,35,000 sq. ft. and scaling capacity utilization at 60% with substantial room to grow [E78, E83]. The operational cash burn noted in March [E28, E29, E30] reversed sharply by the subsequent quarter, with the business generating approximately INR30 crores of operating cash flow as management delivered on self-sufficiency [E86]. Furthermore, the implementation of a zero-salary promoter compensation model linked entirely to dividend distributions from operating cash flows completely realigns governance and mitigates skin-in-the-game dilution concerns [E87].

Conceded: [E86]. The bull claims that operating cash burn completely reversed by the subsequent quarter [E86], but this single quarter of positive cash flow does not erase the severe structural cash destruction of a -0.16x cash conversion ratio and negative free cash flow of Rs -140 Cr for the full year ending March 2026 [E28, E30]. While the bull dismisses the valuation multiples [E1, E2, E11], a 36.1 P/E and an EV/EBITDA of 30.1x against a sector benchmark of 13.83x leave no margin for operational missteps, especially when the price already runs 81% up its 52-week range [E1, E5, E11]. Conceded: [E87]. Although management adopted a zero-salary promoter model tied to dividends [E87], this does not offset the troubling reduction in promoter ownership from 62.08% down to 51.74% [E35]. Furthermore, borrowings continue to climb to Rs 964 Cr alongside net debt of Rs 540 Cr [E33, E88], exposing the business to heightened margin pressures from gold price volatility [E89] while supporting lofty multi-year revenue ambitions [E71] that outpace historical delivery.

Conceded: [E28, E30]. While the full year ending March 2026 recorded a negative operating cash flow of Rs -45 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -140 Cr [E29, E30], the business has already rebounded by generating approximately INR30 crores of operating cash flow in the subsequent quarter [E86]. The bear points to a 36.1 P/E and 30.1x EV/EBITDA [E1, E11], but these multiples are supported by explosive fundamental growth, including 3-year compounded sales and profit growth of 76% and 144% [E14, E16]. Conceded: [E35]. Although promoter holdings decreased from 62.08% to 51.74% [E35], institutional confidence surged dramatically as foreign and domestic holdings rose to 4.70% and 12.44% respectively, backed by a positive institutional money flow signal [E36, E37, E38]. Furthermore, rising borrowings to Rs 964 Cr [E33] are fueling a massive expansion to a 1,35,000 sq. ft. footprint [E78] and an ambitious INR8,100 crores revenue target for FY27 [E71], while utilization sits efficiently at 60% with substantial room to grow [E83].

Conceded: [E86]. While the subsequent quarter reported positive operating cash flow [E86], a single quarter does not erase a full-year cash burn of negative Rs -45 Cr in operating cash flow and negative Rs -140 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E29, E30], resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.16x [E28]. The bull dismisses rich multiples, but a P/E of 36.1x [E1], EV/EBITDA of 30.1x [E11], and a price-to-book of 10.30x [E2] heavily outpace sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], meaning the aggressive 76% sales growth and 144% profit growth [E14, E16] are already fully baked into a volatile stock showing 69.6% annualised volatility [E48]. Conceded: [E36, E37]. Despite rising institutional participation [E36, E37], promoter holdings have structurally dropped by 10.34 percentage points down to 51.74% [E35], which flags a long-term insider divestment trend of -21.8% over three years [E57]. Finally, expanding borrowings to Rs 964 Cr [E33] to fund ambitious capacity targets [E78] leaves the balance sheet encumbered with a heavy net debt level of INR540 crores [E88], creating vulnerability if gold price volatility continues to squeeze industry margins [E89].
